questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why robots in films are often violent
How robots are being used to wash the dishes and babysit children
How to build a robot at home
A friendly robot designed to keep lonely people company
questions.why: They discuss companion robots, especially Abi, who is making friends with elderly people in Melbourne.

questions.q: How does Neil feel about living with a robot?
options: He would love one to help him with all the cooking and housework
He doesn't want one because his house is busy enough
He already has one at home
He would only want one for his children
questions.why: Neil says he doesn't want to live with a robot because he has enough people in his house.

questions.q: Which reports about robots does Beth mention?
options: People sharing secrets with robots and even falling in love with them
Robots replacing most doctors in hospitals
Robots refusing to follow human orders
Children learning to read and write much faster with help from robot teachers
questions.why: She mentions people telling secrets to robot therapists and falling in love with robot friends.

questions.q: What gave Grace Brown the idea to build Abi?
options: A Pixar film she watched as a child
A request from a care home in Melbourne that needed more staff
Spending five months alone during the Covid pandemic
Her job as a nurse for elderly people
questions.why: She had no human contact for five months during Covid and built Abi to help other lonely people.

questions.q: Who are Andromeda's robots mainly designed for?
options: Elderly care home residents who get few visitors
Busy parents with young children
Engineers who work alone
Hospital patients who are recovering from Covid and feel lonely
questions.why: The robots are made as company for elderly care home residents who don't get many visitors.

questions.q: According to Grace, what surprises people when they meet Abi?
options: How quickly she can clean a room
How quiet and shy she is
How much she looks like a real adult
How much personality and independence she seems to have
questions.why: Grace says people don't expect so much personality and feel she's 'got a mind of her own'.

questions.q: Why did Grace make Abi child-sized, colourful and similar to cartoon characters?
options: To make her cheaper to build
So that people would feel relaxed and not afraid of her
Because she was mainly designed to be used in schools and nurseries
So she could be sold as a toy
questions.why: Her softer design was chosen so children and elderly people could interact with her naturally and without fear.

questions.q: How does Beth react to the story of Abi?
options: She still finds robots frightening
She thinks Abi is too expensive
She is pleased to hear something positive about robots
She worries that families will stop visiting their elderly relatives
questions.why: Beth says it's good to hear the positive side of a technology that can seem strange or frightening.
